rationale: Three-lens review of the FAQ Git datasource MR (commit b99abc927, origin/main..HEAD). Acceptance lens: all 9 FRs, 5 acceptance scenarios, and every 'Selected approach' decision PASS with diff evidence. One decision_needed finding blocks: CR-001 — the shared BaseLLMRoutingDatasourceProcessor.get_documents_by_checksum, which the LIVE Google Docs routing path uses, was changed from one-directional startswith to bidirectional match; this is an intentional fix for the LLM echoing full TOC lines, but it also over-fetches parent sections for hierarchical references and is not covered by a Google regression test, so a human must confirm the FR-8 'no Google regression' tradeoff. Deferred (not emitted, non-blocking): multi-head alembic hygiene (b2c3d4e5f6g7 and two other siblings branch off f1g2h3i4j5k6; the merge 06c3e0359af9 reconciles only b2c3d4e5f6g7+b1c2d3e4f5a6 — referenced revisions all exist and the merge is structurally valid, verify heads==1 before deploy); parser robustness on lone-CR line endings, block-scalar heuristic false positives, unreachable binary-decode skip branch; add_header_to_chunks=False may drop header context on size-split of large sections; fetch_remote_stats upper-bound count vs skipped files; normalize_faq_path accepts '..' segments (indexes nothing rather than escaping) and the update route does not 422 degenerate faq_path like create does; files_filter bypasses faq_path 422 validation. Dismissed (3): timezone AttributeError (mixin provides the field), reindex/update authz gap (both call _validate_project_change, consistent with Google routes), broken migration chain (parents exist).

findings.title: get_documents_by_checksum matching widened to bidirectional — changes live Google Docs routing (FR-8)
findings.problem: The Google reference match changed from one-directional `doc["reference"].startswith(ref)` to bidirectional `doc_ref.startswith(ref) or ref.startswith(doc_ref)` (plus .get/strip/skip-empty). The docstring justifies it as fixing the routing LLM echoing full TOC lines (ref longer than the stored reference), which the old code would miss entirely. But the extra `ref.startswith(doc_ref)` direction now also matches every reference that is a string-prefix of the routing ref — e.g. routing to "1.1" additionally pulls the parent "1". This is a real semantic change to the LIVE Google Docs whole-document routing path, which FR-8 requires to have no regression, and the acceptance lens mischaracterized it as a verbatim move.
findings.impact: Google Docs routing over-fetches parent sections for hierarchical/prefix-colliding TOC references, changing retrieved-context composition for an existing feature. Net effect (echo-fix benefit vs over-fetch cost) depends on Google's reference format and is not covered by any regression test in this diff.
findings.recommendation: Human decision required (decision_needed): either (a) consciously accept the widening as an intentional routing fix and add a Google-path regression test that pins the echo case AND the parent/prefix-collision behavior; or (b) tighten the match to be delimiter/segment-aware (e.g. match on exact ref or ref + boundary separator) so a short parent reference does not swallow child-section routing. Confirm against real Google TOC reference formats before merge.
